* Toronto equities will take their cue from U.S. employment data out before the bell. * If numbers are steady or unexpectedly weak, market will rally; if not, it will fall.
Toronto stock watchers are awaiting this morning's U.S. employment numbers, out before the open, to determine Friday's direction.
"It's really going to hinge on the data," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie. "The 8:30 (EDT/1230 GMT) report will certainly set the tone for the day."
The U.S. will report non-farm jobs numbers and the unemployment rate, both for July.
Yesterday the Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index gained 26.73 points to reach 6877.30, its 31st record finish this year.
If the figures stay static or weaken, investors will again take the market to new highs, Beattie said.

Softer numbers will ease concerns that the U.S. economy is growing too quickly, forcing the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates which would increase pressure on the Bank of Canada to follow suit.
"If the data comes in stronger than expected, look for a pull-back," Beattie added.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Air Canada, the nation's largest airline, posted second quarter profits of C$0.44 versus year ago C$0.69.
* Oils were steaming yesterday. Shares in Suncor, Canada's fourth largest integrated oil firm, jumped 7.20, or nearly 19 percent, to 45.65 in active trading.
